dataDefects.title: Ionic balance error outside tolerance
dataDefects.detail: Balance error is -91.8 % against an acceptable ±5 %.

dataDefects.title: Entered TDS contradicts the sum of ions
dataDefects.detail: TDS entered 280000.0 mg/L, but the listed ions already sum to 132875.7 mg/L.

dataDefects.title: Seasonal variation
dataDefects.detail: This tool works from a single set of values.

substitutions.why: At 280 000 mg/L the osmotic pressure is about 218 bar, which is above the pressure rating of every leachate membrane made. The plant the sheet describes cannot be built by any membrane route. 20 000 mg/L is the middle of the published range for mature landfill leachate.
Free chlorine cannot coexist with 35 000 mg/L of COD — it would be consumed in seconds. The figure is a mislabelled chloride, and even as chloride it is nearly seven times seawater.

substitutions.parameter: Na, K, Ca, Mg, SO4, HCO3
substitutions.why: None of the major cations appear in the sheet, so no ionic balance can be computed from it. The set used here is typical of mature leachate and is internally neutral; it is an assumption, not a measurement.

The sheet gives ammonia but no total nitrogen, so organic nitrogen is unknown. Taking TN equal to the ammonia is the optimistic case: any organic nitrogen present is not strippable and would raise the final effluent nitrogen.

caseA.name: Case A — laboratory sheet as written
caseA.feedName: Landfill leachate — literature composite, as tabulated

units.label: Coagulation
notes: Raw water alkalinity is low; pH control will be active and caustic demand significant.

units.label: UASB
notes: Biogas recovers about 3062 kW of thermal energy. Whether that is a credit depends on there being something on site that can use it — on a landfill with a waste-to-energy plant it is; on a standalone leachate plant it usually is not, and the gas is flared.
Volume is set by the organic loading rate (3938 m3), not by the HRT (1164 m3). On strong wastewater this is normal.

units.label: Alkali Dosing pH 11
notes: Ammonium accounts for 100 % of the alkali demand. Sizing the dose from alkalinity alone would under-order the reagent several times over.
Lime adds calcium to the water. Where the next step is a membrane, check the concentrate saturation before choosing it over caustic.

units.label: Ammonia Stripping
notes: The diameter is set by the air, not the water: 20.1 m2 is needed to keep the gas below 2 m/s, against 1.9 m2 for the liquid. The actual liquid loading is only 2.4 m3/m2.h. This is why a stripping tower designed from the water flow alone comes out far too small.

10.3 t/d of ammonium sulphate is produced. That is a fertiliser with a real market, but it needs offtake, storage and logistics — and the matching sulphuric acid supply chain — before it can be counted as a credit.

units.label: Neutralisation pH 7
notes: Neutralising before a membrane is not optional. At high pH the ammonia is a dissolved gas and passes reverse osmosis almost freely; at neutral pH it is the ammonium ion and is rejected above 95 %.

units.label: MBR
notes: Nitrification needs 1303 mg/L of alkalinity as CaCO3 and only 0 is present. The pH will crash, nitrification will stall, and the plant will fail on ammonia while looking like a biology problem. Dose alkalinity or accept a lower ammonia removal.

BOD:TN is 2.77, far below the 3-4 that denitrification needs. The nitrogen removal set here is not achievable without external carbon, and on a high-TN leachate that carbon bill is usually the reason the biological route is abandoned in favour of stripping.
BOD:COD is 0.13, so most of the COD is refractory and no biology will touch it. A COD removal above about 20 % is not credible on this water.

units.label: DTRO 2-stage
notes: Estimated feed pressure 840 bar exceeds the 120 bar module rating. Either the recovery is too high for this salinity or the water is too concentrated for DTRO at all — check the feed TDS before anything else.
Feed osmotic pressure alone is 218 bar. A membrane cannot work below its own osmotic pressure, so at this salinity the answer is evaporation, not more pressure.
Concentrate reaches 1838 g/L. That is at the practical ceiling for DTRO; taking it further needs an evaporator or a brine concentrator.

units.label: Catalytic AOP
notes: Effluent BOD rises from 0 to 2 mg/L as refractory molecules are broken into biodegradable fragments. Useful ahead of a biological polishing step; a compliance problem if this is the final unit.

Ammonia Stripping: 60.0 t/d of ammonium sulphate is produced. That is a fertiliser with a real market, but it needs offtake, storage and logistics — and the matching sulphuric acid supply chain — before it can be counted as a credit.

Neutralisation pH 7: Neutralising before a membrane is not optional. At high pH the ammonia is a dissolved gas and passes reverse osmosis almost freely; at neutral pH it is the ammonium ion and is rejected above 95 %.

MBR: BOD:TN is 2.69, far below the 3-4 that denitrification needs. The nitrogen removal set here is not achievable without external carbon, and on a high-TN leachate that carbon bill is usually the reason the biological route is abandoned in favour of stripping.
MBR: BOD:COD is 0.13, so most of the COD is refractory and no biology will touch it. A COD removal above about 20 % is not credible on this water.
DTRO 2-stage: Concentrate reaches 131 g/L. That is at the practical ceiling for DTRO; taking it further needs an evaporator or a brine concentrator.

Catalytic AOP: Effluent BOD rises from 0 to 2 mg/L as refractory molecules are broken into biodegradable fragments. Useful ahead of a biological polishing step; a compliance problem if this is the final unit.
MVR Evaporator: Verify scaling and boiling point elevation with a rigorous thermal model before committing.
